newsitem.title: UK: Clean tanker rates firm, but increases slow.
newsitem.headline: Clean tanker rates firm, but increases slow.

text.p: Product tanker fixing improved this week and rates were overall a touch firmer.
Activity was largely dominated this week by trans atlantic trade - gas oil moving from the U.S. to Europe.
Shipbrokers estimate that around 570,000 tonnes of U.S. gas oil will head to Europe during October and that more may be on the way.
Rates were assessed around W100 on 60,000 tonnes with cargoes of 68,000 seen going at W82.5 and 40,000 at W140.
In the Caribbean up U.S. coast market itself 30,000 tonners have edged up slowly with as high as W220 done. Refineries running at near capacity prompted an increased need for tonnage.

The Middle East Gulf was also firmer as delays led to cancellations and a scramble to pick up remaining tonnage. Brokers said 55,000 tonners carrying naphtha to Japan were now at W175-180 having stumbled around just below W170 for several weeks.

Mediterranean chartering continued apace this week with demand outweighting suitable tonnage. Naphtha carriers were able to secure a little under W200 while gas oil tankers settled happily around W170.
UK/continent business rose during the week and rates went with it, brokers said. Tankers carrying 20,000 tonnes of product were now able to command up to W220.
